einzeiler: Exploring how college majors correlate with political ideology and religious beliefs.
kurzfassung: Guest Ryan Burge discusses new data analyzing how college majors reflect students' political leanings and religious habits. The conversation covers the distinct clustering of majors, from conservative finance students to liberal arts majors. Listeners then call in to share how their own career paths align with or defy these data trends.
stichpunkte: Ryan Burge presents data from Fire surveying 68,000 college students across 250 universities about their majors, politics, and religion.
Finance, accounting, and business majors emerge as the most conservative and most religious groups on campus.
Arts majors, including theater, fine arts, and English, lean strongly liberal and report the lowest levels of religious affiliation.
Data shows that English majors have a notably low percentage of students identifying as heterosexual, linking sexual orientation, politics, and religion.
Nursing and pre-med majors present an interesting outlier, combining high religiosity with more centrist or moderate political views.
Demographic data on race and religiosity reveals that African Americans are the most religious group in the US, followed by Latinos, whites, and Asians.
Callers ring in to discuss whether their own college majors and professions—such as nursing, business, and social work—match the study's findings.
beschreibung:
Can your college major predict your politics—or even how religious you are? Michael talks with Ryan Burge, a professor of practice at Washington University in St. Louis’ John C. Danforth Center on Religion and Politics, about fascinating new data showing sharp differences among finance, nursing, English, theater and other majors when it comes to ideology and religiosity. Then listeners call in to see whether they fit the stereotype—or completely break the mold. Original air date 17 August 2026. Hosted by Simplecast, an AdsWizz company. See https://pcm.adswizz.com
